messages:
sara: quick design sync idea — introduce a lightweight 'crossover holdback' escape hatch during A->canary migrations. small fraction stays on old path while we validate telemetry.
joel: can you sketch the behavior? how is it different from a normal holdback?
sara: main diff: automated eviction + sampling probes that can shrink or expand holdback without manual rollback. goal: detect subtle regressions faster while minimizing blast radius.
kishore: sounds useful. need clear contract: what metrics trigger eviction vs alert? and who owns the decision loop?
marta: propose two signals: safety (errors, p50/p95 spikes) and quality (evaluation set regressions). safety -> immediate evict, quality -> staged shrink/expand.
alex: quick strawman rollout policy (pseudo):
```
{
  "mode": "crossover-holdback",
  "holdback_fraction": 0.03,
  "probe_window_s": 120,
  "safety_thresholds": {"error_rate": 0.01, "p95_latency_ms": 1200},
  "quality_eval": {"dataset": "smoke-prompts", "max_regression": 0.02},
  "failover": "immediate"
}
```
sara: yes — plus a sampling layer to surface tail cases. e.g., route 0.1% of holdback to mirrored canary for deep evals.
joel: operationally, where does the decision live? control plane? runtime? both?
kishore: split responsibilities: runtime enforces routing and quick safety evictions (SOFT/IMMEDIATE), control plane runs quality evals and issues gradual policy changes. keep safety path as local runtime circuit.
marta: tradeoffs: local runtime eviction is low-latency but limited visibility. control plane decisions are richer but slower. we should support both with a simple interface: 
```
RolloutController.observe(metric, value)
RolloutController.request_adjustment(policy_delta)
```
alex: agree. also need idempotent audit logs so customer can see why an eviction happened (trace id -> metric snapshot).
sara: how about a small proto for the decision event? {kind: EVICT|SHRINK|EXPAND, reason: "p95>t", snapshot_id: "..."} — simple enough to wire into Console.
joel: fallback model selection — do we prefer pin-to-version or route to last-known-good?
kishore: prefer last-known-good candidate with version pin in the rollout state. avoids stale bugs in older models.
marta: open question: can we allow user-defined quick-scripts to run on EVICT events (e.g., roll to customer-specific fallback)? security implications.
alex: +1 to operator hooks but gated by enterprise policy. keep default simple.
sara: ops/telemetry: expose per-rollout tokenized traces, p95/p99, error histogram; retention of 30d for triage. also metric backfills for small holdbacks to validate stats.
joel: ok. next steps: draft RFC with 1) runtime circuit contract 2) control plane decision loop 3) audit/event schema 4) minimal console surfaces. I'll carve the runtime section. sara you can own telemetry/audit. kishore will own quality-eval integration.
sara: assigning owners in doc. quick sync tomorrow 11am PT?
kishore: works for me.
marta: works.
devops-bot: deploy-notification: created #canary-holdback-rfc draft branch: git.redwood/infra/rollouts/crossover-holdback.
sara: thanks — i'll link the draft in the meeting invite.
